use_when: Use it when a person must enter one piece of information, such as an email or a check-in date.
Use the helper for a single constraint, or for the reason a value failed.
Use Error when the value has to change. Use Warning when it can be submitted and the risk should be called out.
Use it on phone screens, where the 52px field is the touch target.
Use the same Error and Warning rules as the desktop field.
Use the helper for one short rule that can be read without scrolling.

dont_use_when.when: Do not use the placeholder as the label. It disappears once the field is typed.
Do not hide the helper until Error. The field will jump.
Do not detach the instance to recolor a status border or status text.
Do not override the field height. It is fixed so inputs align in a row.
Do not write the label in all caps or end it with punctuation.
Do not shrink this field to the 40px desktop height.
Do not drop the label unless the screen already names the value.

variant_intent.variant=Primary: Use it when a person must enter one piece of information, such as an email or a check-in date.
variant_intent.variant=Mobile: Use it on phone screens, where the 52px field is the touch target.
variant_intent.State=Hovered: Hovered — pointer is over the field. Border shifts to brand.
variant_intent.State=Typed: Typed — the field holds a value.
variant_intent.State=Error: Use Error when the value has to change. Use Warning when it can be submitted and the risk should be called out.
variant_intent.State=Warning: Use Error when the value has to change. Use Warning when it can be submitted and the risk should be called out.
variant_intent.State=Disabled: Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.
variant_intent.Show Label: Label and Helper text are text properties, each with a Show toggle. Turn either off when that line is not needed.
variant_intent.Show Helper text: Label and Helper text are text properties, each with a Show toggle. Turn either off when that line is not needed.

placement: Stacked in a form, one field per row with its label above: 'Full Name', 'Email' and 'Password' in the Figma 'Component Appearance' examples, with a Primary button below.
On phone screens the Mobile variant is the touch target (Figma, Input Field/Mobile).

a11y.fact: The label is a real <label> bound to the input with htmlFor and id.
State=Error sets aria-invalid; Warning does not, because the value can still be submitted.
With the label hidden, the input keeps an accessible name through aria-label.
The helper is tied to the input with aria-describedby.
State=Disabled sets the real DOM disabled attribute.
Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.
Keyboard focus is not in this set yet. Do not treat hover as a substitute.
